notes.title: Keep Living your Witchy Life in Endless Mode!
notes.notes:
[h2]Endless Mode Update[/h2]

Happy Autumn, Everyone!

Not only is Witchy Life Story 15% off for the Steam Autumn Sale event, but we've also added a new game mode for those of you who have completed the game! In [b]Endless Mode[/b], you can...
[list]
[*] Craft all the spells and enchanted items from the main game
[*] Create custom spells using any combination of ingredients
[*] Created custom enchanted objects by clicking on the item in your grimoire that you wish to enchant
[*] Tend your garden to keep collecting ingredients
[*] Decorate your altar and do tarot readings
[*] Keep dressing up your witch anyway you like
[/list]
We also changed the moon clock to run on a 28-day cycle for those who like to base their magical practices around the moon! No matter what ending you got for the harvest festival, you should be able to access Endless Mode from the title screen once you complete the game. Of course, let us know if you run into any issues! We'll do our best to help :)

And, of course, if you enjoyed Witchy Life Story, be sure to leave us a review! It's a small way that helps indie games like ours!

notes.title: An update, some fixes, and a big THANK YOU!
notes.notes:
[h2]Thank you![/h2]

First of all, a big THANK YOU to everyone who bought, played, streamed, shared, and reviewed our game this past week. Without your support, our launch wouldn't have been such a success!!! And if you enjoyed Witchy Life Story but haven't had the chance to review it yet, please do! 

[b]Reviews are a great way to keep supporting games like ours! :)[/b]

[h2]Now for the update...[/h2]

We've been seeing some folks asking for an endless mode in Witchy Life Story where you can keep crafting spells after you completed the main game. We're happy to announce we're working on it!

As of now, we're thinking after you finish the main game, a button will appear on the title screen that takes you to the endless mode. Here you can keep crafting spells using recipes from the game, but also new ones based off whatever ingredients you want to use! You'll also be able to access the character creator if you just want to play dress up, along with your altar so you can keep decorating and doing tarots readings. Of course you'll have access to the garden and village shop too when you need to get more spellcrafting supplies!

[h2]Oct. 11th Bug Fixes & Updates [/h2]
[list]
[*] Minor spelling and grammar error
[*] Achievements should all now unlock
[*] Fixed dialog text issue where last few words would get cut off
[*] Fixed *some* of the resolution issues. Text and screens should resize properly, but some stuff needs to be worked out still. See "know issues" below.
[*] Divination Oil should now unlock on the player's altar
[/list]
[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] Depending on the resolution, the player's witch doesn't size correctly
[*] Depending on the resolution, the options menu and some other UI elements don't clear correctly when closed.
[*] Depending on the resolution, the mouse cursor duplicates itself in the garden
[/list]

As always, if you find any bugs or issues, let us know! Feel free to post them in the "Bugz" discussion here on steam, or email us at info@sundewstudios.com!

notes.title: Let's make some witches!
notes.notes:
Happy Halloween Everyone!

If you’ve been watching our [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@sundewstudios?lang=en]TikToks[/url] and [url=https://www.instagram.com/sundewstudios/]Instagram[/url] feed, you’ve probably seen our character creator previews this month. So I thought it’d be fun to give you all a first look at our character creator in-game for our October newsletter! We’ve been working on this feature for a year now, and it feels great to show it off finally. I knew from the start that I wanted [i]Witchy Life Story[/i] to have a character creator, so planning started early in the development process. Every member of our four-person team contributed to this feature, just to give an idea of just how much work and love went into it. So keep reading for a behind-the-scenes look into the creation of our character creator and how it all looks in-game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/1d040181fbfae9af2c6f34b1b8de674ff771bd5a.gif[/img]

Yes, before we get into it, I realize the “Moles” checkbox is not aligned with the rest of the checkboxes. I said we’re still working on it, right??

Anyways! As I mentioned above, we’ve been working on the character creator for about a year now. We started with figuring out the key customization options we wanted to support. We decided on different body types and skin colors relatively quickly. The other big one was making sure all hats worked with every hairstyle, which meant we’d need a system where certain hairstyles would need “alts” that would turn on if the player selected a hat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/cf27c527f3558d323b176f60a41e7a89e27248d2.gif[/img]

After that, Aubrey, our programmer, got to work on all the tech behind the character creator. I worked with Sara to start figuring out how many options per customizable option we should have… We very quickly realized just how much art we were going to need to make this thing work. We wanted 18 skin tones and nine outfits for each of the five body types, which meant Sara would have to draw all these options. Fortunately, we figured out how to tint skin tones in Unity (and then used this tech for all the hair, eyebrows, and lips, too), which significantly cut down the workload. However, even though different colors got taken care of, for the most part, there was still a ton of assets to draw.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/eda440c56e66db1ca5937cbdf938759bf1ae76e8.gif[/img]

Inclusivity was super important to us, so even though it meant there was a lot to draw, we would go ahead with it. Sara spent about seven months working on the assets for the character creator. They worked on other parts of the games (all our beautiful backgrounds and villagers!) during this time too, but the character creator was the bulk of the work. It’s hard to show off just how many options we’ve put into this feature because there are just so many! But I think that’s a good problem to have.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/26f66b8d8686b7cf88ae1dbe5a23567ce786c985.gif[/img]

But if you want a rundown of all the customizable features…

[list]
[*] 5 body types + 18 skin tones
[*] 30 hairstyles + 27 colors
[*] 11 eyebrows + 27 colors
[*] 13 eyes + 7 colors
[*] 9 noses
[*] 10 mouths + lip option in 8 colors
[*] 16 hats and hair accessories
[*] 9 outfits
[*] Plus things like blush, freckles, moles, body hair, etc.
[/list]
We’ve implemented most of the options into the game, but we’re still working on lips... Lips are oddly a unique feature and need some special programming magic to work…! We’re also planning to add hat colors and a few more outfits. And of course, there’s still some ironing out to do to make sure everything looks and works the way it’s supposed to.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/a973990992c225157ee763b26bdceae9a3616330.gif[/img]

So what’s left?

Other than odds and ends, honestly probably the most exciting part of the character creator. Right now, Aubrey is working on getting the character expressions up and running. This means the witch you create will be a full-fledged character with a range of emotions. We’re also trying to figure out a way for you to change your appearance (and names and pronouns) mid-game if you feel like switching things up a bit.

That’s all we have for now! But since it’s Halloween, here’s a little nightmare fuel for you. This is a screenshot from the character creator prototype while we figured out how to tint colors in unity. I think Lianne’s UI looks much better!!!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/b082b8fd4ee10c0b453a115d93c8f22fb2f82e67.png[/img]

notes.title: August 2021 Witchy Life Story Updates!
notes.notes:
[h1]Witchy Life Updates[/h1]

[h3]Happy August, Everyone!

Is it already August?! It’s been a pretty busy summer over at Sundew Studios. I think I can say people received [i]Witchy Life Story[/i] pretty well during Wholesome Direct back in June. So many people tweeted about the game and wishlisted it on Steam. I was kind of in a state of shock that whole week! Then in July, some [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@laelindria/video/6987110557010693382]content creators[/url] over on TikTok [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@video.kames/video/6987905220340698374]made videos[/url] of our game! I’m so glad people are enjoying [i]Witchy Life Story[/i]. Honestly, the response has been a little overwhelming! And I feel like we’ve barely shown off any of the game… There’s still one romance option to introduce (along with several other villagers), plus our pretty extensive character creator… Seriously. That thing is a beast. More details are below, but I’m so impressed with how far it’s come. Anyways, thank you so much for all your support. I genuinely appreciate every tweet, TikTok, wishlist, like, follow, and newsletter sign-up. Now to just finish the game!

Cheers,
Allie, Founder & Creative Director[/h3]


[h2]Writing[/h2]

[h3]Other than Wholesome Direct, I’ve been pretty radio silent on all the things we’ve been working on for the past two months. That’s mainly because I spent that time getting a ton of writing done. Every villager has five main requests, and the first three are kind of the “core” ones that establish who the villager is and what problems they’re having. Also, during those requests, the player chooses how to shape their witch’s rotten personality. Finally, after several rewrites, and in some cases, massive overhauls, they’re done! By “done,” I mean they still need some editing and probably more rewriting, but they’re in a good solid draft state. Now all that’s left is writing the remaining requests, romance and friend events, and the ending… NBD. [/h3]

[h2]Character Creator[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/f96ad383f76a05d73e6d55cb6c2e10beba187530.png[/img]

[h3]Other than writing, Aubrey’s been hard at work getting the character creator up and running. There’s a preview of the character creator in the trailer, and it’s so close to being done. We’re wrapping up some UI stuff and pronoun implementation right now. After that, we’ll finally get to add in all of Sara’s super cute witchy features for your witches! After seeing all of Aubrey and Sara’s work, this character creator could honestly be its own game. Below you can see a sample of some of the choices you’ll have in terms of skin colors, body types, hats, and hairstyles. We’ve tried to give you as many choices as our small team can! Hopefully, we’ll get to show the finished character creator soon! [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/f8db1f0e282d8063b04ed089a4b0810c89a4b084.jpg[/img]

[h2]Crafting[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/13b880af667630115306ba32a988010f2f33d06b.png[/img]

[h3]I’m also in the process of updating Witchy Life Story’s crafting system. Before, the player would receive a letter from a villager and guess what spell to craft from that letter. It felt kind of unintuitive and also didn’t incorporate much in terms of plant lore. So now, when you receive a letter, you go through a simple interactive moment where you uncover the spell type, the color of the second ingredient, and the planetary alignment of the third ingredient. I also worked this ability to discover spell ingredients into your witch’s backstory, so hopefully, the new system feels more tied to the game world. [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40353871/353095de5644ba155e35b5baa96dffb2611f31cb.jpg[/img]
